acceptance: 1) In real isolated PostgreSQL, concurrent acquisition of the same key yields only one success; after a 90s lease, a new generation can acquire it. Completion by an old owner/generation is rejected and cannot overwrite new results. 2) summary accepts only allowlisted counts/times/versions; lastSucceededAt advances only on successful commit, and failure retains the old successful time. There is no arbitrary-script execution capability. M5-T8 wires this primitive into real jobs at the production composition point.
